name: LlamaIndex
description: Open-source Python data framework for building LLM applications over private data: data connectors, indexing/structuring tools, and advanced retrieval/query interfaces for RAG and agentic apps.
features: Data connectors for APIs, PDFs, docs, SQL and more
300+ integration packages for LLM, embedding, and vector-store providers
note: Company focus has shifted toward LlamaParse; the OSS framework remains available (MIT) per its README.

name: LangChain
description: Open-source framework for building agents and LLM-powered applications, with a standard interface for models, embeddings, vector stores, retrievers, and composable chains.
features: Standard interfaces for models, embeddings, vector stores, and retrievers
Large integration library for real-time data augmentation
LangSmith for evals, observability, and debugging

name: Haystack
description: Open-source AI orchestration framework for building production-ready LLM applications in Python, with modular pipelines and agent workflows with explicit control over retrieval, routing, memory, and generation.
features: Modular pipelines with retrieval, ranking, filtering, and routing components
Agent lifecycle hooks and built-in tracking of steps, token usage, and tool calls
Native async support and token-by-token streaming

name: RAGFlow
description: Open-source RAG engine (Apache 2.0) that fuses RAG with agent capabilities as a context layer for LLMs, with a web UI and APIs for document ingestion, chunking visualization, and agentic retrieval.
features: Agentic retrieval with Low/Medium/High/Ultra thinking modes
Template-based chunking with visualization and human intervention
Knowledge compilation into Wikis, Graphs, Trees, Mind Maps, and Timelines
Multiple recall paired with fused re-ranking

name: Verba
description: Community-driven open-source RAG chatbot application (BSD-3-Clause) powered by Weaviate, offering an end-to-end interface for retrieval-augmented generation with local or cloud LLM providers.
features: Hybrid search combining semantic and keyword search
Support for Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, HuggingFace, Groq, and more
Multiple chunking techniques (token, sentence, semantic, recursive, code, JSON)
note: Discontinued by Weaviate; repository archived and read-only, no further updates.

name: txtai
description: All-in-one AI framework (Apache 2.0) for semantic search, LLM orchestration, and language model workflows, centered on an embeddings database combining vector indexes, graph networks, and relational storage.
features: Embeddings database unifying sparse/dense vector indexes with graph and SQL querying
RAG pipelines with citations, plus GraphRAG and speech-to-speech RAG examples
Agents built on smolagents connecting embeddings, pipelines, and workflows
Web and MCP APIs with JavaScript, Java, Rust, and Go bindings

name: R2R
description: Advanced AI retrieval system (MIT) for agentic RAG with a RESTful API and Python/JS SDKs, including a Deep Research API for multi-step reasoning over a knowledge base and the internet.
features: Hybrid search (semantic + keyword) with reciprocal rank fusion
Multimodal ingestion of txt, pdf, json, png, mp3, and more
Knowledge graphs with automatic entity and relationship extraction
User and access management with authentication and collections

name: RAGatouille
description: Library (Apache 2.0) for easily using and training state-of-the-art late-interaction retrieval models (ColBERT) in any RAG pipeline, covering training, indexing, and document retrieval with strong defaults.
features: Train and fine-tune ColBERT models with built-in training-data processing
Create compressed, on-disk ColBERT indexes from documents
Search indexes with ranked results including content, scores, and metadata
Integrations with Haystack, LlamaIndex, LangChain, and Vespa
note: Repository renamed/moved from bclavie/RAGatouille to AnswerDotAI/RAGatouille; canonical URL used here.

name: LangChain4j
description: Idiomatic open-source Java library for building LLM-powered applications on the JVM, with a unified API over LLM providers and embedding stores and easy agents and RAG pipelines in Java.
features: Unified API over 20+ LLM providers and 30+ embedding (vector) stores
Toolbox spanning prompt templating, chat memory, function calling, agents, and RAG
Dedicated easy-rag module for RAG pipelines
Integrations with Quarkus, Spring Boot, Helidon, and Micronaut

name: fastRAG
description: Research framework (Apache 2.0) for efficient retrieval-augmented generative pipelines, providing optimized embedders, rankers, and ColBERT/PLAID components compatible with Haystack.
features: Optimized int8 bi-encoders and sparse cross-encoder rankers
ColBERT token-based late interaction with PLAID indexing
Fusion-in-Decoder and REPLUG generative multi-document components
note: Archived by Intel Labs; no maintenance, bug fixes, or new releases. Included as a historically notable RAG research framework.

name: Pinecone
description: Fully managed proprietary vector database built for AI, with instant-write indexing and fast vector queries at scale, managed through a console or terminal.
features: Fully managed vector database with no infrastructure to operate
Automatic indexing with no tuning required
Enterprise governance, compliance, and reliability controls

name: Weaviate
description: Open-source, cloud-native vector database written in Go that stores objects and vectors together, combining vector similarity search with keyword filtering, generative (RAG) search, and reranking in a single query interface.
features: Advanced hybrid search combining semantic and keyword (BM25) search
Built-in generative search (RAG) and reranking capabilities
Automatic vectorization at import via integrated embedding models
Horizontal scaling, multi-tenancy, replication, and RBAC

name: Qdrant
description: Vector similarity search engine and database (Apache 2.0) written in Rust, providing a production-ready service to store, search, and manage points (vectors with JSON payload).
features: Dense, sparse, and multi-vector search including ColBERT-style late interaction
Rich payload filtering combined with hybrid search fusion (RRF, DBSF)
Built-in vector quantization with tunable speed/precision trade-offs
REST and gRPC APIs, distributed deployment with sharding and replication

name: Milvus
description: High-performance, cloud-native vector database (Apache 2.0) built for scalable ANN search, organizing and searching vast amounts of unstructured data with a distributed, Kubernetes-native architecture.
features: All major vector index types (HNSW, IVF, FLAT, DiskANN) with GPU indexing support
Hybrid search combining dense vectors with native full-text/BM25 and sparse embeddings
Real-time streaming updates with horizontal scaling and high availability
Multi-tenancy, RBAC, TLS, and hot/cold storage tiers

name: Chroma
description: Open-source data infrastructure for AI (Apache 2.0) centered on embeddings search, with a minimal 4-function Python/JS API that runs in-memory, persisted locally, or as a client-server deployment.
features: Core API of four functions: create_collection, add, query, get
Automatic tokenization, embedding, and indexing with optional custom embeddings
Metadata filtering and persistence from in-memory prototyping to server mode
Managed Chroma Cloud service alongside the open-source engine

name: pgvector
description: Open-source vector similarity search extension for Postgres, storing vectors alongside the rest of relational data with exact and approximate nearest neighbor search under Postgres ACID semantics.
features: HNSW and IVFFlat approximate nearest neighbor indexes
Single-precision, half-precision, binary, and sparse vector types
L2, inner product, cosine, L1, Hamming, and Jaccard distance operators
ACID compliance, point-in-time recovery, and JOINs with relational data

name: Elasticsearch
description: Distributed search and analytics engine that also serves as a vector database, supporting near-real-time search over massive datasets including vector search and RAG integrations.
features: Vector search and hybrid retrieval for RAG use cases
Full-text search alongside vector search in one engine
Distributed RESTful architecture with language clients
Kibana integration and managed deployments on Elastic Cloud
note: Elastic's server-side source code is under Elastic License/SSPL terms, not an OSI open-source license.

name: OpenSearch
description: Open-source, Apache 2.0 distributed search and observability suite; a community-driven fork of Elasticsearch used for search over unstructured data at scale.
features: Open-source distributed and RESTful search engine
Apache 2.0 license with Linux Foundation governance

name: Vespa
description: AI search platform (Apache 2.0) for search, inference, and organizing vectors, tensors, text, and structured data at serving time and any scale, used by large internet services serving high query volumes.
features: Unified search, ranking, and ML inference over vectors, tensors, and text at serving time
Designed for sub-100ms query latency over continuously changing corpora
Free trial cloud deployments plus self-hosted operation

name: Typesense
description: Fast, typo-tolerant search engine (GPL-3.0) positioned as an open-source alternative to Algolia, Pinecone, and Elasticsearch, supporting vector search, semantic/hybrid search, and built-in conversational RAG.
features: Vector search on embeddings with nearest-neighbor retrieval
Semantic/hybrid search with built-in embedding models or external providers
Conversational search (built-in RAG) generating answers over indexed data
note: GPL-3.0 licensed; check license implications for commercial use.

name: LanceDB
description: Developer-friendly open-source embedded retrieval library (Apache 2.0) for multimodal AI built on the Lance columnar format, running locally or in the cloud for vector, full-text, and SQL search.
features: Vector similarity, full-text, and SQL search over multimodal data
Built on the Lance columnar format for storage and analytics
Automatic versioning and zero-copy data management
Python, Node.js, Rust, and REST SDKs with LangChain/LlamaIndex integrations

name: FAISS
description: Library (MIT) for efficient similarity search and clustering of dense vectors, developed at Meta's Fundamental AI Research group, with indexes scaling from in-memory to datasets that do not fit in RAM.
features: L2, dot product, and cosine similarity search with exact and approximate indexes
GPU-accelerated indexes as drop-in replacements for CPU indexes
Compact quantization codes scaling to billions of vectors on a single server
C++ core with complete Python/numpy wrappers

name: GraphRAG
description: Microsoft Research graph-based RAG system that extracts structured data from unstructured text to answer complex questions over private data.
features: Structured data extraction from unstructured text
note: Official README states the project is largely in maintenance mode (no new features or PRs, bug fixes and dependency updates only) and is a research demonstration, not an officially supported Microsoft offering.

name: LightRAG
description: Lightweight graph-based RAG implementation designed to be simpler and faster to set up than full GraphRAG pipelines. MIT-licensed and actively maintained.

name: nano-graphrag
description: Compact, minimal GraphRAG implementation intended as a small, hackable codebase for experimenting with graph-based retrieval. MIT-licensed.
features: Local, global, and naive query modes

name: HippoRAG
description: Neurobiologically inspired long-term-memory framework for LLMs that builds knowledge graphs from documents to support multi-hop retrieval. MIT-licensed.
features: Qdrant, ChromaDB, and Milvus vector stores

name: Self-RAG
description: Adaptive retrieval framework that trains a single language model to retrieve on demand and critique its own retrieved passages and generations using reflection tokens.
features: Critiques retrieved passages and generated output

name: Corrective RAG (CRAG)
description: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation: adds a lightweight retrieval evaluator that triggers corrective actions, such as web search or document filtering, when retrieval confidence is low.

name: RAPTOR
description: Tree-organized retrieval: recursively embeds, clusters, and summarizes text chunks into a tree so retrieval can happen at multiple abstraction levels.
features: Recursive embedding, clustering, and summarization of chunks

name: HyDE
description: Zero-shot dense retrieval method: an LLM generates a hypothetical document answering the query, which is embedded and used to retrieve real documents from the corpus.
features: Embeds it as the query vector
Retrieves real documents from corpus embedding space

name: FLARE
description: Active retrieval augmented generation: the model decides when and what to retrieve during generation, predicting the upcoming sentence and regenerating when confidence is low.
features: Decides when and what to retrieve during generation

name: Ragas
description: Open-source LLM evaluation framework with objective metrics, test-set generation, and production feedback loops for RAG and agent applications. Apache-2.0.
note: Repository transferred/renamed from explodinggradients/ragas to vibrantlabsai/ragas; use the new canonical URL.

name: DeepEval
description: Open-source LLM evaluation framework with pytest-style assertions, 50+ ready-to-use metrics (including RAG, agent, safety, and conversational metrics), and synthetic dataset generation. Local-first, Apache-2.0.

name: Promptfoo
description: Open-source toolkit for testing LLM prompts across providers with assertions, metrics, and red teaming. Ships as CLI, library, and CI integration.

name: Phoenix
description: Open-source AI observability platform from Arize AI with OpenTelemetry tracing, response and retrieval evaluations, versioned datasets, experiments, and prompt management.

name: FlashRAG
description: Python research toolkit for RAG with modular retrievers, rerankers, generators, and compressors, plus preprocessed benchmark datasets and ready-made advanced RAG implementations.

name: BERGEN
description: End-to-end benchmarking library for reproducible RAG experiments, supporting many retrievers, rerankers, LLMs, metrics, and QA datasets through a simple YAML/Hydra configuration system.
note: Released under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial use only).

name: RGB
description: Bilingual (English/Chinese) benchmark for RAG LLMs measuring noise robustness, negative rejection, information integration, and counterfactual robustness.
note: Code and data released under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial use only).

name: KILT
description: Benchmark unifying 11 knowledge-intensive language tasks (fact checking, entity linking, slot filling, open-domain QA, dialogue) grounded in a single Wikipedia snapshot, with provenance evaluation.
note: Repository is archived (read-only); datasets remain available via Hugging Face.

name: BEIR
description: Heterogeneous information-retrieval benchmark with a common framework for evaluating NLP-based retrieval models across diverse IR datasets (17 preprocessed datasets per the README), covering dense, lexical, sparse, and reranking architectures.
features: Lexical, dense, sparse, and reranking evaluation
NDCG, MAP, Recall, Precision, MRR metrics

name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
description: Foundational 2020 paper introducing RAG: parametric seq2seq memory combined with non-parametric dense retrieval over Wikipedia, fine-tuned end-to-end with retrieved documents as a latent variable. Set state of the art on three open-domain QA tasks.
features: Dense Passage Retriever over Wikipedia index
State-of-the-art on three open-domain QA tasks

name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
description: Comprehensive survey organizing RAG into Naive, Advanced, and Modular paradigms, covering indexing, retrieval, generation, augmentation techniques, and evaluation frameworks.

name: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
description: Empirical study showing LLM performance on multi-document QA and key-value retrieval degrades when relevant information sits in the middle of long contexts; best at the beginning or end. Directly motivates reranking and context ordering in RAG.
features: Multi-document QA and key-value retrieval analysis

name: Ragas: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
description: Introduces Ragas (Retrieval Augmented Generation Assessment): reference-free metrics for evaluating RAG pipelines across retrieval, faithfulness, and generation quality without human-annotated ground truth.
features: Separate retrieval, faithfulness, and generation dimensions

name: Seven Failure Points When Engineering a Retrieval Augmented Generation System
description: Experience report from three case studies (research, education, biomedical) cataloguing seven failure points in engineering RAG systems and arguing robustness emerges through operation rather than upfront design.
features: Seven failure points: missing content, missed top-ranked docs, not in context, not extracted, wrong format, incorrect specificity, incomplete

name: Contextual Retrieval
description: Anthropic's official technique for improving RAG retrieval: prepending LLM-generated, chunk-specific context before embedding (Contextual Embeddings) and indexing (Contextual BM25). Reported to reduce top-20 retrieval failures by 49%, or 67% when combined with reranking.

name: sentence-transformers
description: Python library for dense sentence/text embeddings, cross-encoder rerankers, sparse encoders, and ColBERT-style multi-vector encoders, with training support and semantic-search use cases. Apache-2.0, actively maintained (original UKPLab/sentence-transformers now redirects here).

name: BGE / FlagEmbedding
description: Retrieval toolkit for search and RAG: embedding and reranker model inference, fine-tuning, evaluation, and tutorials. BGE-M3 supports dense, sparse, and multi-vector/ColBERT retrieval over long multilingual inputs (up to 8192 tokens).
note: The BGE reranker family is maintained inside this same toolkit repository.

name: E5
description: Microsoft's family of text embedding models (English, multilingual, unsupervised, and LLM-based) shipped with BEIR/MTEB evaluation scripts in the official unilm repository.

name: Voyage AI Embeddings
description: Commercial embedding API with Voyage 4 general, lite, large, and code models, plus finance and legal models; offers query/document input types, selectable dimensions, quantized output types, and an open-weight voyage-4-nano model.

name: Cohere Embed
description: Commercial embedding API (embed-v5.0-pro) for semantic search, classification, and clustering, with multilingual support, text/image/mixed-content embeddings, Matryoshka dimensions, and float/int8/uint8/binary/ubinary output types.

name: Jina Embeddings v3
description: Multilingual, multi-task open-weight embedding model supporting 8192-token sequences, five task-specific LoRA adapters, and Matryoshka truncation from 32 to 1024 dimensions.
note: Licensed CC BY-NC 4.0; commercial use requires a separate arrangement.

name: Nomic Embed v2
description: Multilingual mixture-of-experts text embedding model with flexible 768-to-256 Matryoshka dimensions and open weights, code, and training data; supports SentenceTransformers and Transformers.
note: 512-token maximum sequence length; query/document prefixes required.

name: Unstructured
description: Open-source library for ingesting and preprocessing PDFs, HTML, Word, images, and other formats for LLM/RAG pipelines: partitioning, chunking, embedding, structured output, connectors, and document-processing MCP support.

name: Docling
description: Document understanding library that parses PDFs, Office documents, and many other formats into a unified DoclingDocument with layout, reading order, table, and formula understanding plus OCR; runs fully locally, even air-gapped, and exports Markdown/HTML/JSON.

name: Chonkie
description: Python chunking library offering token, sentence, recursive, semantic, late, code, neural, LLM, table, and fast chunkers, plus chunking pipelines, a REST API, embedding providers, and vector-store integrations.
note: Canonical repository moved from chonkie-inc/chonkie to feyninc/chonkie.

name: MinerU
description: PDF and document extraction tool with OCR and four parsing tiers, supporting PDF, images, Office, OpenDocument, EPUB, OFD, HTML, and CSV with structured outputs and stable page/block locators. The README states MinerU is not a RAG framework.
note: GitHub reports its license as NOASSERTION (unclear/custom).

name: SPLADE
description: Learned sparse retrieval method that uses a BERT MLM head for query/document expansion, enabling explicit lexical matching over an inverted index; ships training, indexing, and retrieval code with pretrained weights and BEIR/PISA evaluation.
note: GitHub reports its license as NOASSERTION.

name: ColBERT
description: Late-interaction retrieval model that encodes queries and documents into token-level embeddings scored with MaxSim contextual late interaction; includes indexing, search, training, ColBERTv2 plus PLAID, and a lightweight search server.

name: ColPali
description: Visual document retrievers that embed document page images directly using vision-language models with multi-vector embeddings and ColBERT-style late interaction, capturing text, layout, charts, and other visual content.
note: Repository moved from vidore/colpali to illuin-tech/colpali; the ColPali Engine package is deprecated while the repository and model family remain active with migration guidance.

name: FlashRank
description: Ultra-lightweight Python reranking library supporting pairwise and pointwise cross-encoder rerankers as well as listwise LLM rerankers. Apache-2.0.
note: Verified canonical path is PrithivirajDamodaran/FlashRank.

name: Cohere Rerank
description: Commercial Rerank API (v2) that takes a query and a list of documents and returns them ordered by relevance score, commonly used as a second-stage ranker in RAG pipelines; supports top_n, max_tokens_per_doc, and document metadata.

name: Voyage Rerank
description: Commercial rerank API (rerank-2.5 family) that scores a query against a list of documents and returns reranking results with relevance scores; supports up to 1,000 documents per request, top_k, return_documents, and truncation options.

name: BGE Reranker
description: Open cross-encoder reranker model family (including bge-reranker-v2-m3) maintained in the FlagEmbedding toolkit for second-stage re-ranking in search and RAG pipelines.
note: The models are distributed via the FlagEmbedding toolkit repository rather than a standalone repository.

name: RankGPT
description: Research paper investigating generative LLMs such as ChatGPT and GPT-4 as re-ranking agents for information retrieval, and distilling their ranking ability into small specialized models via a permutation distillation scheme.
note: Full title: 'Is ChatGPT Good at Search? Investigating Large Language Models as Re-Ranking Agents'.

name: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)
description: Paper defining Reciprocal Rank Fusion, a simple unsupervised method for combining document rankings from multiple IR systems that consistently beats any individual system and the standard Condorcet Fuse baseline. Presented at SIGIR 2009.
note: No arXiv version exists; the DOI above is the official ACM record for the SIGIR 2009 paper.

name: Do Current Retrievers Cover All the Evidence? A Controlled Study of Conjunctive Cross-Page Retrieval
description: Controlled benchmark study of conjunctive cross-page retrieval using n-Clue, which tests whether retrieved documents cover every requested condition.
features: Measures complete-first success for multi-condition cross-page retrieval

name: ReinPool: Reinforcement Learning Pooling Multi-Vector Embeddings for Retrieval System
description: Reinforcement-learning framework that filters and pools token-level multi-vector embeddings into compact, retrieval-optimized representations without manual importance annotations.
features: Inverse-retrieval training objective with NDCG-based rewards
Evaluated on ViDoRe V2 across three vision-language embedding models
Compresses multi-vector representations into single vectors

name: Annotation-Free Reinforcement Learning Query Rewriting via Verifiable Search Reward
description: RL-QR trains query rewriting without human-annotated rewrites using verifiable search rewards derived from index-aligned synthetic queries.
features: Annotation-free reinforcement learning for query rewriting
Derives rewards from index-aligned synthetic queries
Evaluated with lexical and semantic retrieval on ViDoRe V2 and MS MARCO v2.1
